item.text: I’ll read the input and check every three-node placement against the constraints and failure scenarios.

item.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -c 'import json,itertools
x=json.load(open(\"input.json\"))
lat={tuple(sorted([a[\"a\"],a[\"b\"]])):a[\"ms\"] for a in x[\"latencies\"]}
valid=[]
for nodes in itertools.combinations(sorted(x[\"nodes\"],key=lambda n:n[\"id\"]),3):
 ids=[n[\"id\"] for n in nodes]; cost=sum(n[\"cost\"] for n in nodes)
 if cost>x[\"budget\"] or any(lat[p]>x[\"max_pair_latency\"] for p in itertools.combinations(ids,2)):continue
 weights=[]
 for s in x[\"failures\"]:
  remaining=[n for n in nodes if n[\"site\"] not in s[\"sites\"] and n[\"provider\"] not in s[\"providers\"]]
  w=sum(n[\"vote_weight\"] for n in remaining)
  if w<x[\"quorum\"] or not any(n[\"writable\"] for n in remaining):break
  weights.append(w)
 else:valid.append((ids,cost,min(weights)))
best=min(valid,key=lambda v:(v[1],-v[2],v[0]))
print(json.dumps({\"feasible_placements\":sorted(v[0] for v in valid),\"selected\":best[0],\"selected_cost\":best[1],\"selected_min_surviving_weight\":best[2]}))'"
